item.title: Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash
item.description: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente said Wednesday he is optimistic Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal will be fit to face England in the Nations League at the weekend. The 19-year-old winger will miss the world champions’ visit to face the Czech Republic in Prague on Thursday with a knee problem and is set to join up with Spain after that game. Yamal played for Barcelona in the 2-1 La Liga win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday and on Monday Spain said he would not travel to face the Czechs. “He got hurt in the last match, he had some discomfort in one knee, he went for the usual treatment, a scan in Barcelona, and they saw he had inflammation and fluid in the knee — that meant he needed rest,” De la Fuente told reporters. “Our medical staff and his medical staff have a fantastic relationship, and I decided that his trip here should be avoided without knowing whether he’d be in any condition to play.” The coach said he had spoken to the winger and his recovery was looking positive ahead of England’s visit to Madrid on Sunday. “He’s doing a series of exercises with his physio and with the club that indicate the recovery is going well,” continued De la Fuente. “We believe, I’m optimistic, that on Friday he’ll be with us.” De la Fuente dismissed the idea that Yamal, who came third in the Ballon d’Or voting in October, has any special privileges compared to his La Roja team-mates. “He has no privileges, and his team-mates are relaxed about it, because we treat everyone the same,” added the coach. “In similar situations we would have done exactly the same for any other player, and the players know that.” – Unstoppable run – Spain have won all four games so far in Group A3 and sealed qualification to the quarter-finals. De la Fuente’s side are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive outings, and the coach said it provided his team with extra motivation. “We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” explained De la Fuente. “None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.” Spain won their previous outing away in Croatia with a brace from Arsenal’s Mikel Merino. The midfielder is frequently used as a substitute by De la Fuente to great effect, with Merino netting vital goals against Portugal and Belgium in the World Cup off the bench this summer. Merino said he would like to be a starter for Spain but he would not kick up a fuss. “Of course, what player wouldn’t like to get (more) minutes?” Merino told reporters. “You’ll never hear me complain about the coach’s decision, I will respect it… but all players want to be important, have minutes and enjoy themselves on the pitch.” The post Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria 2027 Election Watch: The Battle For The Ballot Deepens As Parties Lose Candidates, Gain Defectors And Confront The Courts
item.description: Nigeria’s 2027 election campaign is entering a phase in which the struggle for political influence is increasingly being accompanied by a struggle for legal recognition. Politicians are changing parties. Campaign organisations are being rearranged. Candidates are withdrawing from tickets. And the courts are being asked to determine who is entitled to contest. But another development is becoming difficult to ignore. Concerns about political violence, misinformation and the safety of electoral participation are growing as the campaign gathers momentum. The latest developments in Sokoto, Kano, Cross River and Ogun illustrate the different pressures confronting political parties. Meanwhile, the African Democratic Congress is fighting to preserve the legal validity of its national leadership and candidate nominations. Atiku’s supporters protesting in Abuja on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 And a new report from the National Peace Committee provides a troubling picture of the campaign environment. Taken together, these developments raise a question that goes beyond the usual calculations about party strength. Will Nigeria’s political parties enter the 2027 elections with settled candidates, functioning organisations and sufficient public confidence in the electoral process? That is today’s Political Signal. SOKOTO: THE DEFECTIONS CONTINUE In Sokoto State, the APC has received another group of defectors from the PDP and ADC. A Sokoto Government House statement issued on November 10 identified three PDP state executive officials, several local-government party chairmen and other political organisers among those who joined the ruling party. ADC ward officials and associated groups were also reported among the defectors. Some reports put the number of departing PDP local-government party chairmen at seven, although the published names clearly identify six. These are party officials, not elected local-government council chairmen. That distinction matters. X/@Aminuchindoo Kano has produced another development involving the ADC. A letter dated November 9 announced the appointment of a 14-member caretaker committee headed by Musa Ungogo. The committee is expected to serve for six months. The appointment comes against the background of earlier disagreements over the party’s state leadership. It also arrives at a particularly sensitive moment for the ADC nationally. The Federal High Court’s November 5 judgment invalidating the David Mark-led national leadership has raised questions about the legal authority behind the party’s nominations. The party has appealed and applied for a stay of execution. However, no appellate reversal or granted stay has been confirmed. The Kano appointment must therefore be viewed in the context of both state-level organisational disagreements and the unresolved national leadership dispute. For now, the appointment establishes a new administrative arrangement. It does not settle every question about the party’s leadership or provide evidence of changing voter preferences. ADC: THE LEGAL BATTLE WIDENS The most consequential national development remains the dispute over the ADC’s leadership and nominations. On November 5, the Federal High Court invalidated decisions taken by the David Mark-led national executive, including the process that produced Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate. The ADC rejected the judgment and subsequently filed an appeal and an application for a stay. Now the controversy has taken another turn. Candidates associated with the party have petitioned international diplomatic missions and organisations, including the United Nations, United States Embassy, British High Commission, European Union and ECOWAS. They are seeking attention to the legal and electoral implications of the judgment and have raised concerns about delays in obtaining its certified copy. The candidates say they intend to pursue lawful remedies. Their petition does not overturn the judgment. Nor does it amount to a stay of execution. And it does not establish that every ADC candidate has been finally excluded from the ballot. But it demonstrates that the dispute is no longer confined to the party’s national leadership. Candidates across different states now have a direct interest in the outcome. For the ADC, the immediate challenge is legal certainty. For INEC, the challenge is determining how to respond to the judgment and any subsequent appellate orders. And for the wider electoral process, the question is whether these disputes can be resolved sufficiently early to provide clarity for parties, candidates and voters. The legal status of a party’s nominations is not the same thing as its political support. That distinction must remain central to our Election Watch. CROSS RIVER: A RUNNING MATE WALKS AWAY In Cross River State, the NDC has suffered a candidate-level setback. Stella Charles Archibong, the party’s deputy governorship candidate, has withdrawn from the ticket and declared support for Governor Bassey Otu’s re-election campaign through the Back to South Movement. The withdrawal became public earlier in the week. NDC governorship candidate John Odey has acknowledged the development and indicated that consultations are continuing. This is different from an ordinary party supporter announcing a change of allegiance. Archibong was part of the governorship ticket itself. Her departure therefore raises immediate questions about the party’s replacement arrangements and the procedures required for recognition by INEC. No replacement has yet been independently verified on the Commission’s published list. For Cross River, the development concerns candidate organisation and nomination continuity. It does not establish how many voters, if any, will change their preferences because of her decision. OGUN: ADEBUTU’S CASE APPROACHES A DECISION A file photo of Ladi Adebutu. X@adiadebutu In Ogun State, the PDP’s governorship nomination dispute is approaching another important stage. The Federal High Court is scheduled to deliver judgment on Friday, November 13, in the case concerning Ladi Adebutu’s exclusion from INEC’s published governorship list. INEC maintains that Adebutu’s name was absent from the PDP membership register originally submitted to the Commission. In its court filings, the Commission says searches of the register identified Adebutu’s running mate but did not establish Adebutu’s inclusion. It also disputes membership documentation subsequently presented in support of his nomination. Adebutu and the PDP reject the basis of his exclusion. These are competing positions before the court. They should not be presented as judicial findings. The forthcoming judgment could determine the next stage of the dispute, although further appeals may remain possible. For Ogun, the immediate issue is whether the PDP can secure recognition of its intended governorship candidate. The political implications will depend on the court’s decision and any subsequent action by INEC. Until then, the party’s ballot-access position remains unresolved. Tanko previously served as Obi’s presidential campaign spokesman during the 2023 general elections, when the former Anambra State governor contested under the platform of the Labour Party (LP). He was also the presidential candidate of the Northern People’s Congress (NPC) in 2019 and became the party’s national chairman in 2023. The SDP on Wednesday inauagurated Yunusa Tanko as the national coordinator of its presidential campaign council for the 2027 general elections. Tanko’s appointment was announced during the inauguration of the party’s presidential campaign council in Abuja. The appointment was also confirmed by Mark Adebayo, Chief Media and Communications Adviser to the Adebayo/Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council. Speaking at the event, Tanko pledged to work with the SDP presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and his running mate, Usman Bugaje, to secure victory in the 2027 elections. Describing the SDP as a left-wing, people-oriented political party, Tanko said it was committed to representing the interests of disadvantaged Nigerians who had been neglected by those in positions of authority. “The SDP is a left-wing political party. For those of you who do not know, we represent the interests of the downtrodden. The SDP represents those people that you neglect on the streets. So, that makes this particular party people-oriented,” he said. Tanko who disclosed that he resigned as political adviser (North) to Peter Obi, presidential candidate NDC on October 30, explained that his resignation followed his appointment to the leadership of the National Consultative Front (NCFront), following the death of Ghali Na’Abba, the organisation’s former co-chairman and former Speaker of the House of Representatives. Tanko said he had reached out to Obi and Seriake Dickson, national leader of the NDC, expressing appreciation for their support during his tenure as coordinator of the Obidient Movement. Tanko who pledged to work with the NCFront leadership and Adebayo, noting that his relationship with the SDP presidential candidate dated back to 2023 and that both shared a commitment to building a better Nigeria, said, “In advancing our political mission to a new Nigeria that works for all, I pledge to remain consistent and committed to our unwavering belief in good governance, justice, equity, national loyalty and dedication, and an unwavering commitment to moving Nigeria from where it is today to a better and more prosperous nation,” he said. item.title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
item.description: The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East, US media reported Wednesday. Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources. US Soccer, the sport’s governing body in the United States, did not immediately confirm the news or respond to AFP’s request for comment. The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran. Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia — which neighbors Qatar — but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US. This season’s Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen. The US is one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years. Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make “use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability”. item.title: Mbappe ruled out of France’s Nations League game against Italy
item.description: France’s captain Kylian Mbappe will miss his country’s Nations League match against Italy with a hamstring problem, coach Zinedine Zidane said Wednesday. Les Bleus take on Roberto Mancini’s Italy in Milan on Thursday as they bid to strengthen their grip on top spot in Group A1, before facing Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday. “He will miss tomorrow, he felt a little pain and we won’t take any risk,” said Zidane. “It’s a shame to lose players but it’s part of the game. I hope that it’s nothing too serious and that he’ll be available for Sunday… It’s just a minor issue.” The Real Madrid forward is back in the France squad for this camp after missing their last three matches through injury. He has already netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season. Mbappe scored the winning goal in Zidane’s first match as coach, against Turkey in September in the Nations League, but had to leave the pitch shortly afterwards due to pain in his left knee. After three wins and a draw in four group games, victory over Italy would see France qualify for the quarter-finals. If Nigeria gets this right, West Africa and Africa will follow,” he said. Hashim linked religious freedom and national security to the credibility of the 2027 general elections, warning that political intimidation, incitement and electoral malpractice could deepen existing divisions. “Free, fair, transparent and credible elections mean no religious violence, no intimidation, no incitement and no rigging,” he said. item.title: Five factors vehicle buyers should consider – Understanding the true cost of ownership in Nigeria
item.description: By Theodore opara Buying a vehicle is a major financial decision, but many Nigerian motorists focus almost entirely on the amount required to acquire one. While the purchase price is an important consideration, it does not tell the complete story of what it takes to own and maintain a vehicle over the years. From routine servicing and parts replacement, to insurance, fuel and unexpected repairs, vehicle ownership comes with recurring expenses that can significantly influence its overall value. For individuals, families and businesses, understanding these costs before making a purchase can help prevent financial surprises and support better decisions. The ownership cost equation Two vehicles with similar showroom prices may have significantly different maintenance requirements and operating costs. One may benefit from an established after-sales network, readily available spare parts and predictable servicing expenses. Another may present challenges when replacement components are required or technical support is unavailable. These differences can influence the overall cost of ownership. For instance, a vehicle that requires expensive repairs or spends considerable time in a workshop may eventually cost its owner more than initially anticipated. For businesses operating fleets, the consequences can be even greater. Every day a vehicle remains unavailable could affect deliveries, customer service, employee movement and revenue generation. Consequently, vehicle buyers should consider not only acquisition costs but also the financial implications of keeping their vehicles operational. Fourth is the availability and cost of replacement parts, including access to qualified technicians. item.title: Hezbollah chief calls Trump’s midterm defeat ‘an opportunity’
item.description: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem hailed on Wednesday President Donald Trump’s recent midterm defeat, describing it as “an opportunity” for his Iran-backed Lebanese movement and other opponents of the US in the region. Trump’s Republican Party suffered massive losses in last week’s elections, in which the Democrats seized control of Congress. The president has admitted that the war he launched with Israel against Iran in February was a key factor in the defeat. “Today, we have a good opportunity. Trump was defeated in the elections… an earthquake has occurred in America,” Qassem said in a speech broadcast live to supporters. “The one confronting Iran, Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen… has lost,” he added, arguing that Trump could “no longer continue as is”. “His defeat has ramifications for us that are in a way positive.” He added that Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu “has been broken” after he too suffered a loss in a recent election. Netanyahu’s bloc fell well short of the 61 seats it needed to stay in power in the October 27 vote, and the Israeli president has since tasked his rival Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government. Hezbollah, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by two wars it waged against Israel since 2023. Most recently, the group drew Lebanon into the broader Middle East war in March by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people. Israel continues to occupy swathes of southern Lebanon. Lebanon and Israel concluded a framework agreement in June under US auspices, providing for the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces and the disarmament of Hezbollah, but its implementation has stalled. Qassem reiterated on Wednesday that he refused to disarm his group before an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon. item.title: ‘Your turbaning comes with responsibility’ – ‎Tinubu tells son Seyi
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ President Bola Tinubu has congratulated his son, Seyi Tinubu, on his turbaning as Dan Zaki Gwandu by His Royal Highness, Alhaji Muhammadu Iliyasu Bashar, the Emir of Gwandu, in Kebbi State. ‎ ‎The President told him that the honour goes with responsibility as the title of Dan Zaki Gwandu carries the values of courage, leadership and service. ‎ ‎The traditional title, which translates to Son of the Lion of Gwandu, was conferred on Seyi Tinubu on Wednesday at the historic Abdullahi Fodiyo Palace in Birnin Kebbi. ‎ ‎President Tinubu thanked the Emir and the Gwandu Emirate Council for the honour, which the traditional ruler described as the first of its kind in the Emirate’s history. ‎ ‎The President noted that the honour carries a responsibility that extends beyond personal recognition and reflects the enduring bonds of friendship, mutual respect and unity among Nigeria’s diverse peoples. ‎ ‎He acknowledged Seyi’s efforts in youth engagement, community development and empowerment, particularly through his involvement with the City Boy Movement and other initiatives supporting young Nigerians. ‎ ‎“As a father, I am pleased to see my son recognised by a traditional institution with such a distinguished history. ‎ ‎“But I also remind him that every honour comes with responsibility. The title of Dan Zaki Gwandu carries the values of courage, leadership and service. I urge him to live up to those values, remain humble and continue to dedicate himself to the well-being of others. ‎ ‎“Our traditional institutions remain important custodians of our history, culture and national unity. I thank the Emir of Gwandu and the good people of Kebbi State for extending this honour to my son,” the President says. ‎ ‎President Tinubu encouraged Seyi to regard the title as a call to deepen his commitment to youth development, peaceful coexistence and service to Nigeria. ‎ ‎He wished him wisdom, humility and strength as he assumes the responsibilities associated with the traditional title. item.title: 2027: ‘I may leave government if we’re not performing’ — Amaechi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Vice-Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, says he is prepared to resign if an Atiku Abubakar-led government fails to perform, making accountability a central part of the opposition ticket’s pitch to voters ahead of the 2027 election. Amaechi made the comment in a recent interview with News Central TV, where he discussed the ADC’s plans and the record he would ask Nigerians to assess when deciding whether to support the party. The former Minister of Transportation said Atiku knew his character and predicted that Nigerians would hail the former Vice-President as a hero within the first year of an ADC government, if elected. “I’m sure the presidential candidate (of the ADC) knows my character that if we’re not performing, I may likely leave government if we’re not performing,” Amaechi said. Asked whether he meant he would be open to resigning as Vice-President if the Atiku-Amaechi ticket failed to perform, he replied authoritatively: “Yes, I’m not joking. But the way the situation is, and the way I know Atiku, our first year in office, he will be hailed as a hero.” Amaechi also said Nigerians would regret not voting for Atiku sooner if he emerges President and when asked whether he would fulfil his promises, Amaechi challenged anyone who said he had made and failed to honour a promise to come forward. He also called on voters to assess his record in previous public offices, including as governor, minister and Speaker. “Atiku will be hailed as a hero. Nigerians will regret not voting for him earlier before before this time,” “Let any Nigerian who said I made a promise to him and I refuse to fulfil come forward. Any Nigerian, that’s one. Two, let this be a referendum on all of us, not just the current administration. Yes, all of us. Let it be a referendum. Go back and say Amaechi was once a governor. Amaechi was once a minister. Amaechi was once a speaker,” he said. The former Rivers Governor further urged voters to judge his record against their own standards and withhold their votes if he did not meet them. “Judge, assess all that I have done in this office. If I don’t meet your criteria, if I don’t meet what can convince you to vote for us, don’t vote for us,” Amaechi said. item.description: Former FIFA boss Sepp Blatter has slammed current chief Gianni Infantino, calling his successor a “dictator” and suggesting he needs psychiatric help, in an interview with Der Spiegel published Wednesday. Blatter, 90, criticised Infantino’s decision to create the FIFA Peace Prize award for US President Donald Trump in the lead-up to this year’s World Cup, hosted in the US, Canada and Mexico. He was also critical of Infantino’s post-World Cup plans to sell off part of the commercial rights of the competition in the future, which was scrapped after a fierce backlash. “FIFA is suffering. It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded,” Blatter told the German magazine. The Peace Prize, he said, was “embarrassing”. “Why would he do something like that?,” Blatter asked. “Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards? That’s madness.” Blatter said it was easy for Infantino to secure support for his own re-election from national football bodies. “‘If you vote for me,’ he tells the national associations, ‘you will get much more money than before.’ “He is a dictator. People in FIFA tell me that no one is allowed to ride in the elevator with him. item.title: Uganda ruling party rejects plan for son to succeed president
item.description: The leadership of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni’s party has rejected his plan to designate his son, known for boasting of kidnapping and torturing rivals, as his successor, five party sources told AFP on Wednesday. The president’s son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, 52, is currently head of the army, and wields huge and growing influence as his 82-year-old father plays a declining role in governing the east African country after four decades in power. “Muhoozi”, as he is widely known, has vowed to run in the next presidential election scheduled for 2031, but many are unnerved by his flouting of the law, and inflammatory posts on social media, where he frequently boasts of torturing opponents in his “basement”. In recent months, he has had political rivals imprisoned, threatened to behead opposition leader Bobi Wine, and forced the closure of the country’s leading independent media group for several weeks. Although Museveni has ruled with an iron grip since 1986, many within his party, the National Resistance Movement (NRM), have voiced concern at the apparent moves to hand power to his son. In a closed-door meeting of the NRM’s executive committee on Tuesday, convened to determine a successor, a vote on the son’s candidacy had to be abandoned as several of the 28 members spoke against the plan and received loud cheers, according to five people present. Four people had voted in favour of the son, three had voted against, by the time the vote was called off, the sources told AFP. “The combative nature of the (army chief) has created uneasiness among some people. He is fighting and threatening people on social media. Let him start convincing people but not using coercive means to capitulate the population,” said one source. NRM vice-chairman Calvin Echodu told Museveni to retire the son from the army and give him a civilian assignment to get acquainted with the population and prepare himself well for leadership,” said another participant. Echodu also reportedly advised the president that he should stand again in 2031 “as his son is not yet ready,” the source added. The attendees say it was an unprecedented show of defiance against the long-ruling president, who first broached the subject of his succession by presenting a paper to the party grandees in late October, in which he suggested his son had the right credentials for the job. In recent days, Kainerugaba has once again drawn attention with bellicose posts on X, threatening Vice President Jessica Alupo with arrest over claims she was involved in a plot to overthrow the government. item.title: Lagos targets 2,000MW power boost by March 2027, engages 22 investors
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni ​The Lagos State Government has announced plans to add 2,000 megawatts (MW) of electricity to its power supply by March 2027, as part of ongoing regulatory reforms and private-sector partnerships aimed at ending chronic power shortages. ​Speaking at the Lagos Energy Summit 2026, themed:“Lagos Energy Evolution: Transforming the Future,” on Wednesday, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Barrister Abimbola Salu-Hundeyin, said reliable electricity remains critical to sustaining the state’s economic growth. ​”Manufacturers, small businesses, and households have continued to bear the burden of unreliable electricity and high energy costs. “Our administration has been intentional about creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive through improved power infrastructure, regulatory reforms, and increased private-sector participation,” Sanwo-Olu said. ​He noted that the state’s market restructuring is designed to establish clear frameworks for licensing, consumer protection, and accountability among electricity providers, while urging stakeholders to move beyond policy discussions to practical solutions. ​Providing further details on the state’s roadmap, the Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Biodun Ogunleye, disclosed that Lagos is currently engaging approximately 22 investors to close energy-sector transactions and is working with federal authorities to resolve outstanding Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) bottlenecks. ​Ogunleye added that the state’s strategy extends beyond generation to strengthening transmission and distribution networks, automating energy assets to curb electricity theft and vandalism, and promoting renewable alternatives such as solar, wind, and hydropower. ​Highlighting the scale of the deficit, the Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, Ibilola Kasunmu, revealed that Lagos, home to an estimated 22 million people with an electricity demand of about 6,000MW—currently receives less than 1,000MW from the national grid. ​She attributed the shortfall to inadequate generation, gas supply constraints, weak transmission infrastructure, and poor collection systems, noting that “the state is leveraging embedded generation, waste-to-energy projects, and a joint technical working committee with the federal government to bridge the gap.” The post Lagos targets 2,000MW power boost by March 2027, engages 22 investors appeared first on Vanguard News .

According to her, United Nations figures showed that approximately 75,000 Nigerian women died from pregnancy and childbirth-related complications in 2023, representing nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths recorded globally. “That is one woman every seven minutes,” she said, describing the situation as alarming, particularly because many of the deaths were preventable. We must also shape the decisions. It is non-negotiable,” she added. She said Nigeria’s maternal mortality ratio of estimated 993 deaths per 100,000 live births was about five times the global average and significantly higher than the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 70 deaths per 100,000 live births. The professor expressed concern that despite the presence of some of the countries best medical facilities in Lagos State, maternal deaths remained unacceptably high, with some communities recording particularly disturbing figures. According to Wright, the tragedy raised critical questions about the ability of primary healthcare facilities to recognise and manage obstetric emergencies, availability of blood, emergency referral arrangements and access to life-saving treatment. She said the incident underscored the need for functional referral systems linking primary healthcare centres with secondary and tertiary hospitals. “Our goal is not just to safely leave you. Our goal is to ensure that everyone who leaves us goes home with her baby or with her babies,” she said. Wright identified obstetric haemorrhage, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, sepsis, unsafe abortion-related complications and ruptured uterus among the major causes of preventable maternal deaths. She also raised concerns about Nigeria’s child health indicators, noting that under-five mortality declined only marginally from 132 deaths per 1,000 live births in 2018 to 110 in 2024. She described the progress as inadequate, especially against the SDG target of 25 deaths per 1,000 live births. The professor further disclosed that Nigeria had an estimated 2.2 million zero-dose children in 2025, more than any other country, warning that the figure reflected the failure of the healthcare system to reach millions of vulnerable children with essential immunisation services. She also highlighted malnutrition, poor access to clean water, household air pollution, adolescent pregnancies and inadequate youth-friendly healthcare services as major challenges affecting vulnerable populations. According to her, women in low-income settlements, adolescent girls, young mothers, children under five and residents of riverine and peri-urban communities bear a disproportionate burden of healthcare inequalities. Explaining the difference between equality and equity, Wright said providing the same healthcare resources to everyone did not necessarily guarantee fairness because individuals and communities had different needs and faced different barriers. “Health is your right. It is not a privilege. It is not a privilege based on your postcode, or based on your purse, or based on your pocket,” she said. She urged MWAN members to adopt underserved communities, strengthen maternal and child health interventions, support nutrition programmes, promote health insurance and monitor the impact of their interventions. She also called for improved funding, adequate medical equipment, increased healthcare personnel and better remuneration to address the impact of the migration of Nigerian doctors. Wright urged female physicians to support younger colleagues through mentorship and professional development, stressing that women must create opportunities for one another rather than compete destructively. “When women physicians lead, women, children, and communities thrive,” she said. Earlier, the President of MWAN, Lagos State Branch, Dr Ime Maria Edwin Okon, said the conference provided an opportunity for women physicians to renew their commitment to improving healthcare access and outcomes for women, children and communities. Okon stressed that women doctors occupied a strategic position in healthcare delivery because they understood the challenges confronting families both as medical professionals and as mothers. “We are mothers in the land. We understand the health challenges confronting women and children, not only from our professional experiences, but also from our engagement with our families and communities,” she said. She advocated greater adoption of artificial intelligence, telemedicine, digital health platforms and other technological innovations to improve healthcare delivery, particularly in Lagos, where population growth continues to put pressure on available medical personnel. The MWAN president also expressed concern over the continued migration of Nigerian doctors, popularly known as the Japa syndrome, urging government to improve hospital infrastructure, equipment and the welfare of medical professionals. “Support the people that are still here, that have not travelled out, by making sure that infrastructure is very okay,” she said. She warned that doctors could become frustrated and seek opportunities abroad if their working conditions and welfare needs were not adequately addressed. Okon also advocated expanded health insurance coverage to reduce out-of-pocket healthcare expenditure, which she identified as a major barrier preventing women, particularly those in rural and underserved communities, from accessing timely medical attention. On women’s professional advancement, she urged female doctors to embrace technology, continuous learning and leadership opportunities. “If they don’t give you a seat on the table, bring your seats.
